focus_area: Frontend display-state derivation, criteria card/count-rail, empty states, action row, button labels & loading/disabled guards, tier metadata, and JobSetupAiSettings wiring

findings.title: Dead `history` prop declared, passed, and never used in JobCriteriaSection
findings.description: Props declares `history: any` (line 22) and JobSetupAiSettings passes it (`<JobCriteriaSection job={passedJob} history={props.history} />`, JobSetupAiSettings.tsx:107), but the component destructures only `{ job }` (line 25) and never references `history`. Navigation to the job description is done via a react-router `<Link>` (line 40), not `history.push`. The prop is harmless dead code (no crash if `props.history` is undefined), but it is unused and slightly misleading.
findings.recommendation: Drop `history` from the Props interface and from the call site in JobSetupAiSettings.tsx:107, since the section navigates with `<Link>` and never touches the router prop.

findings.title: isInFlight includes react-query isFetching, so the Regenerate button briefly disables on any background refetch
findings.description: `isInFlight = isPayloadStatusInFlight || isFetching` (line 70) drives both `loading` and `disabled` on the action button (lines 160-161). `isFetching` is true for ANY background refetch (e.g. react-query's default refetchOnWindowFocus), not only the post-regenerate refetch, so tabbing away and back momentarily shows the Regenerate/Generate button in a loading+disabled state even though no extraction is running. This is spec-sanctioned (SPEC 8.3 defines isInFlight as 'payload status in-flight OR ... the query is refetching'), so it is spec-compliant, not a defect — recording only as a minor UX observation. Note it also correctly prevents any double-submit, which is the important behavior.
findings.recommendation: No change required (spec-compliant). If the transient loading flash is undesirable, gate on the mutation's own refetch rather than global isFetching.
